question:
With reference to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It proposes a Central Government-appointed "designated authority" in which foreign contribution, and assets created out of it, shall provisionally vest when an FCRA certificate is cancelled, surrendered or otherwise ceases to have effect.
2. It has been referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee of 31 members, comprising 21 members of the Lok Sabha and 10 members of the Rajya Sabha.
3. It provides that no investigation for an offence under the Act shall be initiated without the prior approval of the Supreme Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Bill's proposed Chapter IIIA creates a Centre-appointed 'designated authority' with provisional vesting of foreign contribution and assets on cancellation, surrender or cessation of a certificate; the JPC notified on 3 September 2026 has 31 members (21 Lok Sabha nominated by the Speaker + 10 Rajya Sabha nominated by the Chairman), chaired by Sanjay Jaiswal. Statement 3 is wrong - the proposed Section 48 amendment requires prior approval of the Central Government, not of the Supreme Court.
subject: Polity & Governance
theme: Regulation of foreign funding of voluntary organisations; parliamentary scrutiny of legislation
micro_topic: Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026; 31-member JPC notified 3 September 2026 under Sanjay Jaiswal; proposed Chapter IIIA 'designated authority' and automatic vesting of assets; Section 48 amendment requiring prior Central Government approval for investigation; FCRA 2010 replacing FCRA 1976; FCRA (Amendment) Act 2020 - no sub-granting, administrative expense cap cut 50% to 20%, designated SBI New Delhi Main Branch account; Articles 14, 19(1)(a), 19(1)(c) and 300A; Entry 10 of the Union List

question:
With reference to the Self-Help Group credit roadmap announced in September 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The national target for 'Lakhpati Didis' has been raised from 3 crore to 6 crore women.
2. The roadmap envisages about Rs 10 lakh crore of bank credit to Self-Help Groups and about Rs 1 lakh crore for individual women entrepreneurs over five years.
3. DAY-NRLM, under which the initiative runs, is administered by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: The Lakhpati Didi target has been raised from 3 crore to 6 crore (about 3.01 crore already certified by early 2026), backed by roughly Rs 10 lakh crore of bank credit to SHGs and Rs 1 lakh crore for individual women entrepreneurs over five years. Statement 3 is wrong - DAY-NRLM is administered by the Ministry of Rural Development, not the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
subject: Society
theme: Women's empowerment through Self-Help Groups; financial inclusion and rural livelihoods
micro_topic: SHG-bank linkage review of 3-4 September 2026; Lakhpati Didi target raised from 3 crore to 6 crore by 2029-30; Rs 10 lakh crore SHG credit plus Rs 1 lakh crore individual women entrepreneur credit over five years; about 10 crore rural women in 91-93 lakh SHGs; DAY-NRLM launched as NRLM (Aajeevika) June 2011 replacing SGSY, renamed 2015, Ministry of Rural Development, 60:40 cost sharing (90:10 for NE and Himalayan States); quarterly virtual and half-yearly physical reviews with SRLMs, RBI and NABARD; District Level Consultative Committees

question: The 'Advisory Committee on Audit Quality, Assurance and Technology', constituted in September 2026, was set up by:
options: (a) The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India under the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949
(b) The National Financial Reporting Authority under the NFRA Rules, 2018
(c) The Securities and Exchange Board of India under the LODR Regulations, 2015
(d) The Comptroller and Auditor General of India under the DPC Act, 1971
explanation: The nine-member Advisory Committee on Audit Quality, Assurance and Technology was constituted by the National Financial Reporting Authority on 4 September 2026 under Rules 15 and 16 of the NFRA Rules, 2018, with an explicit mandate covering risks from data analytics, automation, AI and machine learning in audits. NFRA itself was constituted in October 2018 under Section 132(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, with appeals lying to the NCLAT.
subject: Economy
theme: Corporate governance and audit regulation; regulators absorbing emerging-technology risk
micro_topic: NFRA Advisory Committee on Audit Quality, Assurance and Technology constituted 4 September 2026; nine members; Rules 15 and 16 of NFRA Rules 2018; third NFRA advisory body after the Technical Advisory Committee (2020, term ended December 2022) and the Advisory Group on Auditor-Audit Committee Resources (July 2024); NFRA constituted October 2018 under Section 132(1) of the Companies Act 2013; Ministry of Corporate Affairs; chairperson plus maximum 15 members; appeal to NCLAT; Standards on Auditing and Standards on Quality Management

question: 'BIO-NIVESH', recently in the news, is:
options: (a) A sovereign fund set up by NITI Aayog for pharmaceutical manufacturing
(b) A single-window regulatory clearance portal for genetically modified organisms
(c) A platform of the Department of Biotechnology to connect biotechnology start-ups with private investors
(d) A national repository of indigenous crop germplasm maintained by ICAR
explanation: BIO-NIVESH was launched on 3 September 2026 by Dr Jitendra Singh as a DBT/BIRAC platform connecting biotechnology and deep-tech start-ups with private investors, designed as a two-way engagement to bridge the 'valley of death' between proof-of-concept and commercial scale-up. Its inaugural edition brought together about 20 start-ups and around 50 investors.
subject: Science & Technology
theme: Biotechnology ecosystem and commercialisation of deep science
micro_topic: BIO-NIVESH launched 3 September 2026 by MoS (IC) Dr Jitendra Singh; DBT/BIRAC platform; about 20 start-ups and 50 investors in the inaugural edition; selection on innovation, stage of development, market potential, scalability and regulatory readiness; 'valley of death'; India's BioEconomy Report (IBER) 2026 released by BIRAC on 19 March 2026 - bioeconomy USD 195.3 billion in 2025, about 18% y-o-y growth, 4.8% of GDP, up from about USD 10 billion in 2014, target USD 300 billion by 2030; biotech start-ups 5,365 (2021) to about 13,000 (2025); BIRAC (2012) under DBT; BioE3 Policy 2024; National Biopharma Mission 2017; RDI Fund

question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Deendayal, Paradip and V.O. Chidambaranar are the major ports recognised as Green Hydrogen Hubs under the National Green Hydrogen Mission.
2. The National Centre of Excellence for Green Ports and Shipping is hosted by The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI).
3. The National Centre of Excellence for Green Ports and Shipping functions under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Deendayal (Kandla), Paradip and V.O. Chidambaranar (Thoothukudi) are the three major ports recognised as Green Hydrogen Hubs under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, and the NCoEGPS is hosted by TERI at its Gwal Pahari campus. Statement 3 is wrong - the NCoEGPS, established in March 2023, functions under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, not the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
subject: Environment
theme: Maritime decarbonisation; green shipping corridors and alternative marine fuels
micro_topic: Review of green shipping corridors by Sarbananda Sonowal at TERI Gwal Pahari, Gurugram, 3 September 2026; Green Fuel Bunkering Hubs at Deendayal, Paradip and V.O. Chidambaranar port authorities; National Centre of Excellence for Green Ports and Shipping established March 2023 under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways and hosted by TERI; Rocky Mountain Institute corridor modelling; Green Hydrogen Hub Ports under the National Green Hydrogen Mission (January 2023, Rs 19,744 crore); Harit Sagar Green Port Guidelines 2023; Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047; Green Tug Transition Programme

question:
With reference to Joint Parliamentary Committees (JPCs) in India, consider the following statements:
1. A Joint Parliamentary Committee is an ad hoc committee constituted for a specific purpose and ceases to exist once it submits its report.
2. For a JPC examining a Bill, members are nominated by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha for their respective Houses.
3. The recommendations of a Joint Parliamentary Committee are binding on the Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: A JPC is an ad hoc (not standing) committee, constituted for a defined purpose and dissolved once it submits its report; members are nominated by the Speaker for the Lok Sabha and by the Chairman for the Rajya Sabha, conventionally in a roughly 2:1 ratio between the Houses. Statement 3 is wrong - JPC recommendations have persuasive, not binding, force; the Government must place an action-taken statement but is not obliged to accept them.
subject: Polity & Governance
micro_topic: Distinction between standing and ad hoc committees; within ad hoc, Select Committee (one House) versus Joint Committee (both Houses); nomination by the Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Chairman; typical 2:1 Lok Sabha to Rajya Sabha ratio; advisory nature of recommendations and the action-taken report; contrast with Department-Related Standing Committees (introduced 1993) and financial committees - Public Accounts, Estimates and Public Undertakings

question:
With reference to the International Maritime Organization (IMO), consider the following statements:
1. It is a specialised agency of the United Nations responsible for the safety and security of shipping and the prevention of marine pollution by ships.
2. MARPOL is the principal international convention covering prevention of pollution of the marine environment by ships from operational or accidental causes.
3. Its 2023 greenhouse gas strategy sets an indicative goal of reaching net-zero greenhouse gas emissions from international shipping by or around 2050.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: All three are correct. The IMO is the UN specialised agency for shipping safety, security and prevention of marine pollution from ships, headquartered in London. MARPOL (the International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships), with Annex VI covering air pollution, is the principal ship-source pollution convention. The 2023 IMO GHG Strategy sets the indicative goal of net-zero GHG emissions from international shipping by or around 2050, with indicative checkpoints for 2030 and 2040.
subject: Environment
micro_topic: International Maritime Organization - UN specialised agency, headquarters London; MARPOL and Annex VI on air pollution from ships; 2023 IMO GHG Strategy with net-zero by or around 2050 and 2030/2040 checkpoints; distinction from UNCLOS (law of the sea) and the London Convention on dumping; relevance to green shipping corridors, green ammonia and green methanol bunkering
